subject: TTFT & streaming requirements - follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@saasify.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: TTFT & streaming requirements (recap + next steps)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Alex — good conversation. Quick recap of the requirements we captured on the call and proposed next steps so we can align engineering and procurement. Please confirm or correct anything I missed.

Summary of requirements
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target: goal is 150 ms for short prompts (customer interactive flows).
- Streaming transport: prefer Server-Sent Events (SSE) due to corporate firewall policy; WebSocket acceptable as fallback.
- Chunk cadence: sub-250 ms preferred; ideally ~200 ms cadence for UI rendering.
- Throughput & concurrency: sustained 200 RPS peak for inference, with ~50 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Payload characteristics: typical prompt sizes ~50-300 tokens; some bursts up to 4k tokens for batch jobs.
- SLOs: 99th percentile TTFT target <= 300 ms as a hard SLO; 95th percentile target <= 150 ms.

What we owe you
- Redwood to validate TTFT numbers with a short, realistic test using your sample prompts (we'll run both hosted and dedicated configs).
- Provide an SLO matrix and recommended deployment (edge routing + caching + model variant pin) for your workload.
- Confirm support for SSE and provide example client code (SSE + JS/Node).
- Draft mutual action plan & estimated cost for a 30-day pilot (Dedicated trial or Hosted + burst).

Proposed next steps
1) Marissa and I will run a quick latency run against a representative prompt set — target to share initial numbers by Monday (2026-05-18).
2) Schedule engineering sync (30-45 min) next week to go over telemetry, auth, and proxy rules (I proposed Tue/Wed in the calendar invite).
3) We'll attach a preliminary SLO matrix and sample SSE client for you to review.

Attachments: brief SLO matrix (redwood-ttft-slo-matrix.pdf) — draft.

Thanks — Aditya
--
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124
From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@saasify.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 08:12:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT & streaming requirements (recap + next steps)

Thanks, Aditya — this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from my side:
- SSE is preferred (we have strict firewall policies that drop long-lived WebSocket upgrades in some corp locations).
- The 150 ms TTFT is the ideal UX target for our primary interactive path; we can accept the 95p/99p distinction you noted (95p <=150ms, 99p <=300ms).
- For throughput: 200 RPS sustained is right; peak bursts could hit 350 RPS for short windows.
- Concurrency: 50 concurrent streaming sessions is our steady-state, but we may need 100 concurrent during flash events.
- Chunk cadence: yes — every ~200 ms gives the smoothest front-end rendering. We prefer frequent small chunks vs. infrequent large payloads.

Action items for Redwood:
- Confirm SSE support and provide sample implementation.
- Run the latency test on a sample prompt set (I attached our internal spreadsheet with baseline numbers).
- Send a preliminary pricing/MAA for a 30-day pilot (we're evaluating both Hosted and Dedicated).

Attachments: SaaSify_TTFT_requirements.xlsx (contains representative prompt set + current baseline).

I'll get procurement and infra aligned on our side; can we aim to have the pilot scope and pricing by EOW (Friday)?

On the calendar invite, I've proposed Wed 2026-05-20 10:00 PT for the engineering sync. If that works, I'll loop in our Platform Eng lead.

Best,
Alex
--
Alex Reed
VP Engineering | SaaSify Inc.
alex.reed@saasify.com | (617) 555-0210
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 08:45:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: TTFT & streaming requirements (recap + next steps)

Appreciate the details, Alex — all clear. A few notes from our side after syncing with Marissa and solutions: 
- SSE support: confirmed. We'll send a lightweight SSE + Node/JS example and a small Python client for your infra team.
- Latency test plan: Marissa will run a 3x run (cold, warm, warm-with-cache) against your prompt set and return 50/95/99p TTFT numbers. Expect this by Monday EOD PST.
- Pilot recommendation: for the profile you described (200 RPS steady, 350 burst, 50-100 concurrent streams) we recommend starting with a small Dedicated reservation for predictable concurrency + Hosted fallback for burst traffic. Drafts and estimated cost will be included in the pilot quote.
- Chunk cadence: we can tune encoding and server-side bundling to push chunks at ~200 ms intervals; Marissa will include cadence guidance in the test notes.

Attached is a short SLO matrix I mentioned (redwood-ttft-slo-matrix.pdf) showing how we translate your targets into observable metrics and recommended alert thresholds.

Next steps:
- Marissa to run tests and attach results + cadence notes (by 2026-05-18).
- I'll follow up with a pilot quote and a short mutual action plan by EOW.
- Confirm Wed 2026-05-20 10:00 PT for engineering sync — please let me know if that is a conflict.

Thanks,
Aditya
